entries.headline: Robo.ai shareholders to vote on 1-for-25 reverse split
entries.dek: The Nasdaq-listed, Dubai-based company set an October 26 meeting on the share consolidation, record date October 14, effective date November 6 if approved.
entries.caption: Robo.ai's board has called an October 26 vote on consolidating its Nasdaq-listed shares twenty-five to one.

sources.title: Robo.ai Inc. Announces Reverse Stock Split and Extraordinary General Meeting on October 26, 2026

unverified_claims: The current share counts, record date, meeting location and effective date are as stated in the company's own notice to shareholders and have not been independently verified.
brief: Robo.ai Inc. (Nasdaq: AIIO), a UAE-based company, said shareholders will vote October 26, 2026 on a 1-for-25 reverse stock split of its Class A and Class B ordinary shares. The record date is October 14, 2026, and the meeting will be held at the Meydan Grandstand in Dubai.

If approved, the company will consolidate 13,817,501 Class A shares and 222,116,290 Class B shares into 552,701 Class A shares and 8,884,684 Class B shares, effective November 6, 2026 at 9:30 a.m. ET under a new CUSIP, G6693P130. No fractional shares will be issued; holders otherwise due a fraction will instead receive a full share.

The company said the split is expected to lift the Class B trading price proportionately, though it gave no assurance the price would reach twenty-five times its pre-split level. Shareholders at the meeting will also vote on authorizing up to 25 million new Class A shares and 280 million new Class B shares.
body: Robo.ai Inc. (Nasdaq: AIIO), a UAE-based, U.S.-listed company, has called an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders for October 26, 2026, to approve a 1-for-25 reverse stock split of all classes of its ordinary shares. The meeting is scheduled for 8:30 a.m. ET (4:30 p.m. Dubai time) at the Meydan Grandstand, sixth floor, in Dubai, with a record date of October 14, 2026.

If shareholders approve it, the split will take effect November 6, 2026, at 9:30 a.m. ET, consolidating every 25 existing shares into one. The company's 13,817,501 Class A ordinary shares would become 552,701 Class A shares, and its 222,116,290 Class B ordinary shares would become 8,884,684 Class B shares. The post-split shares will trade under a new CUSIP, G6693P130, the company said.

A reverse stock split reduces the number of shares outstanding by combining multiple shares into one, without changing a shareholder's proportional stake in the company other than for fractional adjustments. Robo.ai said no fractional shares will be issued under the proposed 1-for-25 split: a shareholder otherwise entitled to a fraction of a share will instead receive a full share.

Robo.ai said it expects the Class B trading price to increase proportionately once the split takes effect, though it gave no assurance the post-split price would reach twenty-five times its level beforehand; the post-split shares will trade under a new CUSIP, G6693P130. The October 26 meeting will also consider increasing authorized share capital by up to 25 million new Class A ordinary shares and 280 million new Class B ordinary shares, and adopting a seventh amended and restated memorandum and articles of association.

Robo.ai is headquartered in Dubai and lists its Class B ordinary shares on Nasdaq under the ticker AIIO. The release sets out the mechanics of the proposed split and the meeting but does not state a reason for the consolidation; completion depends on shareholder approval, and if approved, the company said the split becomes effective November 6, 2026.

entries.headline: NXG Cushing Midstream Energy Fund to rename, broaden mandate
entries.dek: The fund's Board of Trustees approved renaming it and broadening its investment policy from midstream energy to energy infrastructure, effective December 18.
entries.caption: The fund's Board approved renaming NXG Cushing Midstream Energy Fund and broadening its investment policy, effective December 18.

sources.title: The NXG Cushing® Midstream Energy Fund Announces Fund Name Change

unverified_claims: The fund's statement that roughly 90% of its net assets already qualify as energy infrastructure investments rests on the fund's own disclosure.
brief: The NXG Cushing® Midstream Energy Fund (NYSE: SRV) said its Board of Trustees approved changing the fund's name to The NXG Cushing® Energy Infrastructure Fund, effective December 18, 2026. The fund's ticker, SRV, and CUSIP, 231631300, will not change, the fund said.

The board also approved changes to the fund's non-fundamental investment policies: the 80% minimum-investment threshold moves from "midstream energy investments" to "energy infrastructure investments."

The fund said that as of October 15, 2026, about 90% of its net assets, plus borrowings for investment purposes, already consisted of energy infrastructure investments, so it does not anticipate any change to its investment approach or rebalancing as a result. No shareholder action is required, the fund said.
body: The NXG Cushing® Midstream Energy Fund (NYSE: SRV), a closed-end fund, said its Board of Trustees has approved changing the fund's name to The NXG Cushing® Energy Infrastructure Fund, effective December 18, 2026. The fund's ticker symbol, SRV, and its CUSIP, 231631300, will remain unchanged, according to the announcement, which was released October 16, 2026, from the fund's Dallas offices.

Alongside the name change, the Board approved amending the fund's non-fundamental investment policies. The fund's rule requiring at least 80% of its assets to be invested in a defined category will shift that category from "midstream energy investments" to "energy infrastructure investments."

The release states that as of October 15, 2026, approximately 90% of the Fund's net assets, plus borrowings for investment purposes, already consisted of energy infrastructure investments, and that the Fund therefore does not anticipate any change to its investment approach or rebalancing of its portfolio as a result of the amendment. No shareholder approval or action is required for either the name change or the policy amendment, the release said.

No shareholder vote or other approval was required for either change, the release said, and investors need take no action; the fund's New York Stock Exchange listing and CUSIP are unaffected. Beyond the name, the policy amendment and the asset figures above, the release discloses no further detail about the Board's reasoning.
